css-compound-selector.name: Use commas to change simultaneous satisfaction into any one of them.

css-siblings.name: Use ~ to make all subsequent paragraphs bold as well

css-not-selector.name: Forgot to limit it to the exhibition label category

css-source-order.name: mistakenly rewrote the entire set of styles and lost the original padding.

css-pseudo-element.name: Forgot content, the browser did not generate a decorative box

css-link-focus-visible.name: always draws outlines and loses the distinguishable state

css-checked-state.name: Use [checked] to cause the newly checked items to not be bold.

css-invalid-state.name: Using :required causes the input to be correct but still prompts an error.

css-font-inherit.name: only inherits font-size, and the font family of the control still uses the default value.

css-rem-em.name: uses rem in the inner margin, causing the two exhibition labels to be the same

css-type-scale.name: sets the character spacing to word spacing

css-ellipsis.name: retains line breaks and no line is truncated in long files

css-background-image.name: lost the original image when using background abbreviation

css-gradient.name: gradient direction from right to left

css-shadow.name: Set the entire card to translucent

css-current-color.name: Write both states into green borders

css-list-marker.name: Directly setting li causes the text to change color.

css-table-borders.name: Using border-spacing: 0 only eliminates the gap

css-custom-properties.name: defines the theme variables to all states, and the cards to be checked are also dyed.
